### Hotel Equities Announces Key Leadership Appointments After Strategic Merger With Springboard Hospitality

July 02, 2025

ATLANTA & HONOLULU – July 2, 2025 — As part of the strategic integration following the merger of Springboard Hospitality and Hotel Equities, the combined hospitality management company announces two key leadership appointments: Albert Smith as Chief Operating Officer of Hotel Equities and Rob Robinson as President of Springboard Hospitality. These executive placements mark a significant milestone in aligning leadership for the organization’s integration post-merger.

“These leadership appointments reflect our commitment to operational excellence and strategic expansion as we continue to unify our platform,” said Ben Rafter, Chief Executive Officer of Hotel Equities. “Rob’s leadership has been instrumental to Springboard’s evolution, and Al brings a proven track record in scaling high-performing hotel portfolios. Together, they will help shape the future of our organization and deliver value to our stakeholders.”

About Albert Smith

Based in Atlanta, Smith now leads enterprise-wide operations for Hotel Equities, with responsibility for optimizing performance across hotels, resorts, and outdoor hospitality destinations throughout the United States, Canada, the Caribbean, and Latin America.

Smith most recently served as President of Hotel Operations at Hotel Equities, where he oversaw the strategic management and growth of the company's hotel portfolio. Prior to joining HE, he was Senior Vice President of Lifestyle Hotels at Highgate, leading a portfolio of independent, full-service luxury hotels across the East Coast. Earlier in his career, Smith held senior roles at Pivot Hotels & Resorts for Davidson Hospitality, Viceroy Hotel Group, SBE Entertainment, and Kimpton Hotels & Restaurants, building a reputation for operational excellence, brand development, and strategic leadership.

With over 20 years of experience in upper-upscale and luxury hospitality, Smith brings a holistic understanding of hotel operations across a range of disciplines, including sales, marketing, revenue management, brand development and talent strategy. His appointment reinforces HE’s commitment to operational strength and scalable growth across all verticals.

About Rob Robinson

Based in Honolulu, Robinson now oversees all aspects of the Springboard Hospitality platform and portfolio, with a focus on driving financial performance, executing long-term growth strategies, fostering a strong company culture, and expanding the portfolio across high-growth markets.

Previously executive vice president of Springboard Hospitality, Robinson originally joined OLS Hotels & Resorts in 2018 as part of its new ownership group and played a key role in the company’s transformation into Springboard. He led the company’s rebrand and spearheaded initiatives that positioned Springboard for national growth.

Robinson’s career spans both the restaurant and hospitality industries, with leadership roles at Kimpton Hotels & Restaurants and Highgate, as well as experience as an entrepreneur, having owned and operated a group of successful restaurants and bars in the San Francisco Bay Area. He remains deeply engaged in both the industry and his local community, serving on the Executive Board of Directors for the Waikiki Improvement Association, the Board of the Hawaii Lodging and Tourism Association, and as Chairman of the Waikiki Beach Special Improvement District Association, which he helped found. He also serves on the Advisory Board for Kapiolani Community College’s hospitality program.

## Hotel Equities Names Albert Smith President, Hotel Operations

Leads enterprise-wide performance across firm’s U.S. and Canada Portfolio

ATLANTA – GA., July 27, 2021 – Today, hotel owner, operator, 
and development firm Hotel Equities (“HE”) announced the 
appointment of Albert (“Al”) Smith as President of Hotel 
Operations. 
In his new role, Smith will report to HE’s, Chief Operating 
Officer, Bryan DeCort and will provide oversight and leadership 
for the group’s growing portfolio of 200+ hotels. “Al is a 
tremendous addition to our team and immediately makes us 
better as we continue to expand and diversify our footprint,” 
said DeCort. “His servant leadership style and balanced 
approach to building high-performing teams adds tremendous 
value to our associates and stakeholders. I couldn’t be more 
excited to welcome Al to the HE family.” 
A 20-year luxury hospitality veteran, Smith has held key 
leadership roles in ground-breaking hospitality companies including Viceroy Hotel Group, SBE 
Entertainment, and Kimpton Hotels & Restaurants. Most recently, he served as Senior Vice 
President of Lifestyle Hotels at Highgate where he oversaw a key portfolio of independent full 
service luxury hotel properties along the eastern seaboard. Prior to that, Smith served as Senior 
Vice President with Davidson Hotels where he helped develop the company’s lifestyle and luxury 
brand; growing their lifestyle portfolio from one single property to over twenty-five. 

“Al is a true professional with a passion for our industry”, said Brad Rahinsky, President & Chief Executive Officer for Hotel Equities. “He is a servant leader in every sense of the word with a tenacious ambition that will drive exceptional results, beginning at the core with culture.” Smith is based in Hotel Equities’ corporate headquarters in Alpharetta, GA.

About Hotel Equities 
(HE) is an award-winning full-scale hotel ownership, management and development firm with a 
portfolio of 210+ hotels and projects throughout the United States and Canada. Fred Cerrone, 
CHA, serves as Founder and Chairman; Brad Rahinsky serves as President and CEO. Hotel Equities 
is an affiliate of 33 Degrees, an integrated management platform combining market knowledge 
and industry experience across a broad range of CRE assets including office, restaurant, retail, 
mixed-use and multi-unit residential. For more information on Hotel Equities, visit 
www.hotelequities.com. 

Albert Smith, President, Hotel Operations

– ### –

### Hotel Equities Strengthens Leadership Team with Key Executive Appointments Across New Divisions 

 November 10, 2025 

Atlanta, GA – Hotel Equities (HE), a leading hospitality operator and developer, announces a series of strategic executive appointments across its Full Service, Focused Service, and Lifestyle divisions. These moves and additions will drive innovation, enhance performance, and help create lasting guest experiences across the portfolio—priorities for HE in generating long-term value for key owners and stakeholders.

“These executives bring exceptional talent and diverse industry experience to their newly created roles,” said Albert Smith, Chief Operating Officer of Hotel Equities. “Their leadership is integral as we continue to strengthen our lifestyle, full-, and select-service divisions across the U.S., Canada, and CALA, enhancing value for our owners and partners. By promoting from within, we’re investing in high performers who will help us grow our portfolio and expand our platform for innovation — from traditional hotels to new concepts like our leading outdoor hospitality brand, Postcard Cabins.”

Newly announced positions include:

Peter Tziahanas, President, Full Service Division

Peter Tziahanas joined Hotel Equities in 2021 and previously served as Executive Vice President of Operations, overseeing key lifestyle and owned assets across the firm’s portfolio. In his new role, he collaborates with internal and external stakeholders to drive operational excellence, profitability, and enhanced guest and employee engagement. Before joining HE, Peter held several multi-unit leadership positions with prominent management groups, including Pivot Hotels at Davidson Hospitality Group, where he successfully led the lifestyle operating vertical.

David Rosenberg, President, Focused Service Division

David Rosenberg joined Hotel Equities in 2020 and most recently served as Executive Vice President of Operations, where he oversaw the deployment of analytics-driven performance dashboards, managed M&A integrations, and led a substantial portion of HE’s multi-branded hotel portfolio. He also guided the company’s entry into the outdoor hospitality segment through the integration of Postcard Cabins into the portfolio. With extensive experience across both full-service and select-service hotels, David has held several executive roles throughout his career, consistently driving revenue growth, market share, profitability, and team engagement.

Becky Vealey, Senior Vice President of Sales, Full Service & Lifestyle Division

Becky Vealey, previously HE’s Vice President of Revenue Generation, now oversees sales strategies for the Full Service and Lifestyle Division. Becky leads a high-performing team of Revenue Managers, Corporate Directors of Sales, and Marketing Executives, driving revenue across a multi-brand portfolio. With over a decade in above-property roles and hands-on experience at the property level, Becky brings a strategic and operational edge in revenue generation and commercial leadership. She is also active in HE’s mentorship initiatives helping grow the next generation of leaders in the industry.

Carol Lobaito, Senior Vice President of Sales, Focused Service Division

Carol Lobaito, formerly Vice President of Sales & Marketing, now oversees strategic initiatives to grow market share, drive revenue, and enhance brand awareness within the Focused Service Division and across HE’s outdoor hospitality portfolio. With over 20 years of experience spanning property-level sales, multi-property oversight, and national brand leadership, Carol excels at collaborating with property teams, ownership groups, and franchise partners. 

Liz Flurry, Vice President of Growth Marketing

Liz Flurry, formerly Director of Marketing and Brand Activation, has been promoted to this new role, in which she develops and executes innovative digital marketing and e-commerce strategies to drive booking conversion across HE’s branded portfolio. Liz brings extensive experience in traditional and digital marketing, social media, reputation management, and brand development, including seven years with Marriott. 

Eve Tronson, Vice President of Marketing, Lifestyle Division 

Eve Tronson joins HE as VP of Marketing, overseeing brand, digital, CRM, and field marketing strategy across the portfolio of lifestyle and independent hotels. With over two decades of hospitality experience, including leadership roles at Viceroy Hotels & Resorts, Eve brings expertise in brand storytelling, performance marketing, e-commerce, and guest lifecycle strategy. She is recognized for her collaborative leadership, cross-functional approach, and data-informed creativity that drive measurable growth.

Brandon Standerfer, Vice President of Distribution, Lifestyle Division 

Brandon Standerfer, promoted to VP of Distribution, brings more than 20 years of experience in revenue management, distribution optimization, project management, call center operations, reservation sales, and process improvement. He has worked across all hotel segments, from economy to boutique lifestyle luxury, and is recognized for his ability to integrate diverse disciplines into cohesive, high-performing strategies that optimize revenue and operational efficiency.

Jennifer Cannistraci, Vice President of Sales, Lifestyle Division 

Jennifer Cannistraci, promoted to VP of Sales, leads strategic growth and brand success across a portfolio of lifestyle assets. With experience at Four Seasons, The Beverly Hilton, Sunset Marquis, and Hotel Amarano, Jennifer combines creativity with data-driven strategy to deliver measurable results and elevate brand presence. Her collaborative approach and business acumen position her to drive continued growth and success for the lifestyle portfolio.

 September 04, 2025 

Hotel Equities (“HE”), a best-in-class hospitality operator and developer, today announced it has been recognized by Marriott International as a Top Performing Franchise Management Company in the United States and Canada for Premium & Luxury hotels for the second quarter of 2025. The recognition is based on leading Intent to Recommend (ITR) scores among hotel management companies operating 8+ Premium & Luxury hotels. ITR is a measure of guest satisfaction across Marriott’s portfolio. 

In addition to the overall company achievement, The Farnam, Autograph Collection in Omaha, Nebraska, from Hotel Equities’ managed portfolio, earned recognition among Marriott’s Top 5 Performing Franchised Premium & Luxury Hotels. 

“Our differentiator is the attention to detail that our associates deliver each and every day, and our guests notice and appreciate,” said Al Smith, chief operating officer of Hotel Equities. “I want to congratulate and express my gratitude to the leaders across our organization who set the standard in excellence and consistently prioritize guest satisfaction and comfort as the baseline of true hospitality. These recognitions reflect the passion, precision, and care our entire organization delivers on behalf of our owners and partners.” 

Two of Hotel Equities’ select service properties in Canada, the TownePlace Suites by Marriott Medicine Hat in Alberta and the TownePlace Suites by Marriott Belleville in Ontario, were also recognized as Top Performers for ITR scores. 

Marriott’s performance metrics, including ITR scores, are vital indicators of a management company’s ability to deliver best-in-class guest satisfaction and financial performance. Hotel Equities’ consistent recognition across multiple categories highlights its proven success in optimizing hotel operations, elevating guest loyalty, and maximizing asset value for ownership groups.

. December 17, 2015

East Lansing, Michigan - December 17, 2015 - In a ceremony on Friday, December 4, 14 students from The School of Hospitality Business at MSU were awarded certification in Hotel Industry Analytics (CHIA). Most of the students are members of The School's Real Estate Investment Club.

“We are pleased that each student passed the exam,” says Dr. A.J. Singh, Hilton Hotels fellow and director of the Hospitality Business Real Estate Investment Management minor. “The study program and test are rigorous; the certification will make our students stronger and more marketable.”

The CHIA is offered through a joint effort between the American Hotel & Lodging Educational Institute (AH&LEI), the International Council on Hotel, Restaurant, and Institutional Education (ICHRIE), and Smith Travel Research (STR). In fact, it is the only hotel-related certification for university students graduating from hospitality and tourism programs.

According to STR, the certification demonstrates a student's “thorough knowledge of the foundational metrics and definitions that are used by the hotel industry.” Recipients have the “ability to analyze various types of hotel industry data and to make strategic inferences based upon that analysis. Certification also confirms a comprehensive understanding of benchmarking and performance reports produced by STR. Recipients have a grasp of the current landscape of the hotel industry, including relevant current events.” The exam tests four content areas: Hotel Industry Analytical Foundations, Hotel Math 101 (metrics used by the industry), Property Level Benchmarking Reports, and Ad-hoc Performance Reports.

“We are always striving to give our students an 'edge' as they begin their careers,” explains Authella Collins Hawks, director of The School's Student and Industry Resource Center (SIRC). “So we complement their classroom education with additional learning experiences such as the CHIA.” In fact, The School's culture places an emphasis on all kinds of educational opportunities for its students, including travel to industry conferences, Dale Carnegie Training, dozens of property tours, over 75 professional development programs on- and off-campus each year, and as many as 100 visiting leaders coming to speak to students annually.

In each of these endeavors, scholarships and endowments established in The School help to cover the costs to students associated with registration, travel, or study materials.

For more information about The School of Hospitality Business, please visit: www.hospitalitybusiness.broad.msu.edu

### Triple Mentoring a Key

. October 14, 2008

ATLANTA, GA, September 20, 2007. Hotel Equities recently launched a leadership program named HELP, Hotel Equities Leadership Program, designed to train candidates for positions in management at the Atlanta-based hotel development and management company. Unique to Hotel Equities in content and format, the program provides a way to help people advance within the company.

HELP includes very intense online, technical and face-to-face training as well as job shadowing. Candidates must learn every department in the company including revenue management, sales, housekeeping management and maintenance.

"In my opinion, HELP is the finest training program in the select service sector of the hotel industry," said Fred Cerrone, President and CEO of Hotel Equities.

HELP is structured as a self-paced program. Most individuals will be able to complete the study and activities within nine months to a year. The present group of candidates meets quarterly for training and every six months for a progress review with Director of Training and Human Resources Tamara Markham.

"This comprehensive program directs each participant to touch every aspect of our business," said Ms. Markham.

Nine HE associates, Operations Managers and Assistant General Managers, participate in HELP at this time. In addition to working with a General Manager at his or her hotel, every participant has contact with both a Brand Team Leader and a mentor who are available for questions and consultation. Participants experience multiple styles of leadership that they can emulate to develop their own style for success.

Triple mentoring, providing training and support from three experienced individuals for each candidate, sets the program apart and provides a key to its success.

"I feel very confident that HELP is providing me with the tools I need to be a great General Manager," said participant Rosa Guerra, Operations Manager, Hampton Inn-Stone Mountain.

Hotel ownership, management, and development firm, Hotel Equities, has been selected as the new management company for seven full and select service hotels owned by Sejwad Hospitality, a family-owned hotel development company based in Columbia, South Carolina.

"We are thrilled to partner with the owners of Sejwad Hospitality to manage these best-in-class hotels," said Joe Reardon, Chief Development Officer of Hotel Equities. "Further expanding our portfolio in the full-service sector is a real focus, and this family has an incredible pedigree of developing first-class hotel assets."

Hotel Equities operates 41 full-service and lifestyle hotels in its portfolio of over 250 total hotels.

The properties, which expand Hotel Equities' reach in the South Carolina market, include five existing hotels and two new properties currently under construction:

- Delta Columbia Northeast - a 180-room full-service hotel with in-house dining at Whiskey Kitchen restaurant. Amenities include on-site convenience store, meeting space, outdoor pool, dry cleaning service

- Sheraton Columbia Downtown - A 134-room hotel located in downtown Columbia featuring a rooftop lounge and bar and Vault Martini Bar

- Moxy - Columbia - A 129-room hotel under construction

- SpringHill Suites - Columbia - A 104-room hotel under construction

- Holiday Inn Express - Garners Ferry - A 100-room hotel located minutes away from Columbia's major business and culture districts, offering free hot breakfast, indoor pool, and fitness center

- Holiday Inn Express - Two Notch - Conveniently located just minutes from Fort Jackson Training Center and Interstate 77 and 20, amenities in this 83-room hotel include free hot breakfast, outdoor pool, fitness center

- Fairfield Inn & Suites Columbia Downtown - A newly renovated 83-room hotel in downtown Columbia offering free hot breakfast, on-site convenience store, and dry-cleaning service

"We are excited about our partnership with Hotel Equities which allows us to leverage best practices to achieve greater outcomes together," said Rick Patel, Principal, Sejwad Hospitality. "Our shared values and commitment to enhancing operational efficiencies through hands-on management will drive growth and opportunity for associates."

### Marriott Honors Hotel Equities with Partnership Circle Award

. June 03, 2009

ATLANTA (June 4, 2009) - Marriott International, Inc. honored Atlanta-based Hotel Equities (HE) with its second prestigious Partnership Circle Award. Fred Cerrone, President and CEO of Hotel Equities, accepted the award that is considered the company's top honor for its owner and franchise partners. Only 11 of approximately 400 owners and franchisees of Marriott properties in North America earned the recognition. Marriott Chairman and CEO, J.W. "Bill" Marriott, Jr. presented the award at the company's conference for select service and extended stay owners and franchisees, held at the JW Marriott Orlando Grande Lakes, in Orlando, Fla.

"This is truly a well-deserved honor that recognizes the outstanding accomplishments of Fred Cerrone and his company," said Joel Eisemann, executive vice president, Owner and Franchise Services and Lodging Development, Select Service and Extended Stay Brands, Marriott International. "Our owners and franchisees are key to Marriott's continued success, and we value the strong partnerships we have with companies like Hotel Equities who live and share our vision for hospitality excellence."

Hotel Equities' accomplishments propelled it into the elite winner's circle. During the past three years, HE associates earned four GM of the Year honors and two Associate of the Year awards for Marriott hotels nationwide. Based on guest satisfaction survey results, the firm earned six Gold and six Silver Hotel awards.

Fred Cerrone serves as president on Marriott's Fairfield Inn Franchise Advisory Council and he sits on the Marriott SpringHill Suites Franchise Advisory Council. Hotel Equities operates three Marriott training hotels and earned Runner-Up and Training Hotel of the Year plus the Connect.U Trainer of the Year. HE's Fairfield Inn-Lumberton, NC was named the Fairfield Inn's Top Operations Hotel last year.

Three of Hotel Equities' hotels earned spots on Lodging Hospitality's Top 100 Performers 2008 list. Recently, HotelWorld Network named Fred Cerrone the Hotelier of the Year 2008.

The Atlanta Business Chronicle named Hotel Equities to the top 10 on its annual list of "Best Places to Work" among all medium-sized companies in Atlanta in 2005 and 2006.

"On behalf of the Hotel Equities team, I am honored to accept this award," said Mr. Cerrone. "We seek to exceed the expectations of our guests, associates and investors with our 'Spirit to Serve' hospitality. We are proud to represent Marriott and its unique portfolio of brands."

Marriott International is a leading lodging company with more than 3,200 lodging properties in 66 countries and territories. The company's Partnership Circle Award honors companies who live Marriott's vision, share a mutual long term commitment, fully embrace Marriott's brand initiatives, focus on associates to create a well managed and engaged workforce, invest in hotel product, and provide outstanding customer service as measured through Marriott's guest satisfaction surveys.

Hotel Equities (HE) is an Atlanta-based full-scale hotel management, development and consulting firm with 43 properties presently in its portfolio. Frederick W. Cerrone, CHA, serves as President and CEO. For more information, visit http://www.hotelequities.com.

. April 04, 2011

Atlanta, GA - April 1, 2011 - Atlanta-based Hotel Equities (www.hotelequities.com), represented by President and CEO Fred Cerrone, and Atlanta-based Premier Hotel Corporation, represented by William D. Bowen, announced an agreement to joint-venture the management of seven hotels in Premier's portfolio. The transition of those hotels to Hotel Equities' management team is effective April 1, 2011 and brings the HE portfolio to 51 hotels.

“We welcome this opportunity for a joint venture and partnership with Premier and Bill Bowen,” said Fred Cerrone. “Premier's group of hotels matches well with our company's management expertise and we will provide value to both guests and owners.”

The Premier Hotel Corporation's portfolio of seven hotels includes the Fairfield Inn-Charlotte, NC; Hampton Inn-Adel, GA; Hampton Inn-Douglas, GA; Holiday Inn-Duluth, GA; Wingate by Wyndam-Albany, GA; The Cabot Lodge, Gainesville, FL and Treasure Bay Hotel & Marina, Treasure Island, FL.

In addition, from this point forward, Premier Hotel Corporation and Bill Bowen will refer management contract candidates to Hotel Equities and, on a non-exclusive basis, will serve as a Development Partner with Fred Cerrone and Hotel Equities in the future.

“Fred Cerrone is an industry expert who has developed an award-winning management, development and consulting firm,” said Bill Bowen. “By combining the expertise and resources of Hotel Equities and Premier, we and our stakeholders will benefit substantially.”

Hotel Equities (HE) is an Atlanta-based full-scale hotel management, receiver, development and consulting firm. Frederick W. Cerrone, CHA, serves as President and CEO. Hotel Equities presently has 51 properties in its portfolio including several bank owned (REO) properties under management. ## Two Boutique Hotels on St. Croix and St. Thomas Win Full Tax Breaks; One to Hire 150 Employees in First Year

The VIEDC Board approved 100% tax incentives for a $12M hotel project on St. Thomas hiring 150 people and an $11M boutique hotel on St. Croix creating 20 jobs, alongside new approvals for St. John Brewers, WWTS, and a management firm ownership change.

Development / Published On July 11, 2025 11:29 AM / Staff Consortium July 11, 2025

Image not found or type unknown

Interior of a boutique hotel, not affiliated with current USVI developments. Two boutique hotel developments—one on St. Croix and another on St. Thomas—were approved for generous tax benefits during the most recent decision meeting of the Virgin Islands Economic Development Commission (VIEDC) on Thursday, alongside amendments for a local brewing

company and other business applications. 
At its July 10 meeting, the VIEDC Governing Board voted unanimously to grant full tax 
exemptions to Historic Heritage Holdings, LLP, which plans to construct and operate a boutique 
hotel on St. Croix, and DV USVI Investment LLLP, which will develop a similar hotel project on 
St. Thomas. The approvals were part of five applications reviewed during the session. 
Historic Heritage Holdings, LLP will develop a hotel under Category III of the VIEDC tax 
incentive program. In addition to the hospitality operation, the company will run a designated 
Category IV service business that provides venture capital management, investment services, and 
family office support. Though headquartered on St. Croix, its clientele will be based outside the 
U.S. Virgin Islands, according to the meeting's summary document. 
To support the venture, Historic Heritage has already formed several wholly owned entities—Z 
Property VI LLC, Z Hospitality I LLC, Z Hospitality II LLC, and 3 Hospital Street LLC—to hold 
title to the hotel property. The hotel will be operated by another of its subsidiaries, Stay At 
Uptown LLC. Additional subsidiaries may be created to manage different aspects of the business. 
The company has committed to investing a minimum of $11 million in the project and hiring 15 
full-time employees within one year of receiving either a Certificate of Occupancy or the signed 
VIEDC Certificate, whichever comes later. An additional five employees will be hired for its 
service business under similar timelines. Employees will have access to training opportunities 
through job-based instruction, online courses, employer-sponsored learning, and programs at the 
University of the Virgin Islands. 
The board voted to grant Historic Heritage 100% of the tax incentives allowed by law for 30 
years, excluding revenues from retail sales, concessions, or room rentals not subject to the hotel 
room tax. Income from services to non-eligible clients, such as certain family office customers 
within the U.S. Virgin Islands, will also be excluded from the benefits. 
On St. Thomas, DV USVI Investment LLLP received VIEDC approval to own and operate its 
boutique hotel under the same Category III designation. Like its counterpart on St. Croix, DV 
USVI will also engage in Category IV services, offering venture capital and investment services 
through family office structures. That business will also be targeted at clients outside of the 
territory. 
DV USVI has pledged to hire 150 full-time employees by the end of the first year of hotel 
operations or within one year of the signing of the VIEDC Certificate, whichever occurs later. The 
project carries a $12 million minimum investment and includes commitments to provide on-the 
job training to staff. The company was granted 100% tax incentives for 20 years, with similar 
exclusions on non-qualifying revenues. 
Also on the agenda was KCV Associates, Inc., d/b/a St. John Brewers, which sought a revised 
certificate of tax benefits to better reflect the full scope of its operations. The amendment confirms 
that the company will own and operate a food processing, bottling, and packaging business 
producing its line of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, sauces, seasonings, and food 
products. The board approved the amended grant, with all previous terms remaining in effect. 
Meanwhile, Global Associates Management, LLC, based on St. Croix, received approval for a 
change in ownership. Michael D. Dunham has retired and transferred his 50% ownership to Dr. 
Steven H. Hardee, who now holds full ownership of the business. GAM was originally granted 
VIEDC benefits in 2019 to operate a Category IV service business offering business management 

and financial consulting. The ownership change was formally recognized and approved by the board, with the existing terms of the certificate remaining unchanged.

Lastly, WWTS, LLC d/b/a Worldwide Tap and Still, a management consulting and distribution company, was granted an extension of time to commence its tax incentives. Initially awarded benefits in July 2023, the company cited the need to finalize logistics and staffing. The VIEDC board gave the company until January 1, 2025, to activate its benefits. If WWTS fails to meet that deadline, its incentives will be voided, and it will be required to submit a new application. All other terms of the original approval remain in place.
